title: Lesson 37 - REST Endpoints: Use-Case-Driven HTTP Action Configuration and Auth
description: Explain, dependent upon customer use case, the configuration and management of HTTP Actions within an integration procedure to securely connect to and process data from external REST/SOAP endpoints, including authentication and request/response mapping.

questions.question: A customer needs to read a single account record from an external REST API by its ID. Which HTTP method and request surface should the consultant use?
options: POST with the ID in the body
GET with the ID in the resource path or query parameter
DELETE with the ID in the body
PUT with the ID in the header
questions.explanation: Reading a resource is a GET, and the record identifier belongs in the resource path or a query parameter. POST creates, DELETE removes, and PUT updates, so none of those fit a read operation.

questions.question: A REST endpoint authenticates with an API key that the documentation says must be sent in a header. Where should the consultant configure this?
options: In the request body of the HTTP Action
In the named credential, so the header is applied to the request
In a Data Mapper Transform action
questions.explanation: The named credential holds the authentication details, including an API key sent as a header, and the HTTP Action applies it. The request body carries data, not auth. Output variables and the Data Mapper handle response data, not request auth.

questions.question: A consultant configures a GET call but the external system returns a 400 and the filter never reaches the endpoint. What is the most likely cause?
options: The filter was placed in the request body instead of query parameters
questions.explanation: GET requests carry data in query parameters, not the body. A body on a GET is ignored or rejected, so the endpoint never sees the filter, producing a 400. The credential, response mapping, and timeout would not cause this specific failure.
